frames.review_note: Acceptable. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch14 row (rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin with no stubble, small gold ear stud). Kayal reads correctly as a bay with black mane, tail and lower legs and no white markings. Minor points: the mud reaches only her fetlocks and cannons rather than her knees, and a plain white banner flies in the right background. It is unlettered, but it is not the Travancore silver-conch-on-red standard and could read as a surrender flag. Caption space: the low-detail grey sky at upper left (between the palm and Nagoji's turban) and at upper centre-right above the bullocks and cannon.

Acceptable. A Dutch hand in a blue cuff with gold buttons holds the paper flat, and a lightly lined woman's hand with gold bangles presses a brass seal into red wax. No face shows. The contract lines are illegible scribble marks, and the wax stick at lower left is blurred with no lettering. The brass oil lamp has an open wick. Hand anatomy is sound (the Dutch right hand's thumb is hidden under the palm). Minor: the flashback wash is a little warmer and more saturated than 1.3 and 1.4, because the blue cuff and red wax keep their colour. It is still muted and ragged-edged. Caption space: the dark low-detail wall across the upper centre, above the hands.

Acceptable. Sepia, ragged-edged flashback of the Colachel shore: burned huts with blackened palm thatch, upturned boats, and three Dutch ships at anchor flying plain red-white-blue tricolours with no monogram. Gun smoke drifts from their sides. No text and no people. Caption space: the wide, low-detail grey sky at upper centre and right.

Acceptable. Full colour, in the same wet paddy, grey sky, cannon and bullock column as 1.1. Varma matches varma-v1 and the campaign court look in the bible: cream-and-gold turban with a jewelled peacock-feather crest, curled moustache, pearl earring, bare chest, cream-and-gold cloth and gold necklaces. He rides at the head of his staff with mud on his legs and cloth, eyes tired and jaw set, as rain begins. His rein hand and the horse's head are sound. Minor: the same plain white background banner as 1.1 appears again (consistent, but not the Travancore standard), and Varma's horse has a white blaze, which is fine because it is not Kayal. Caption space: the low-detail rainy sky at upper left (above the palms and cannon) and upper right (above the hills).

Clean. High-angle siege: revetted trench lines with palm-trunk and mat work curve toward the Dutch beachhead, batteries smoking, blue-coated mass pressed against the surf, and a plain red-white-blue tricolour with no lettering. The open sky is only a narrow band across the top (x 0.33-1.0, y 0-0.10), so the longer second caption may need to sit lower right over the sea, or bottom left on the plain sand of the foreground trench wall (x 0-0.25, y 0.78-1.0).

Clean. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch13-15 bible row: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, talwar, thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and a gold ear stud. Dhanaji matches his sheet: white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, short black beard, no sash, talwar at the hip, stockier and shorter, and he wipes his brow with his fist. A fresh smoke plume rises over the Dutch camp, and its plain tricolour matches 2.1. Hands are sound. Dhanaji's two balloons fit in the open sky above and between the heads (x 0.30-0.75, y 0.02-0.25).

Acceptable. Ponnan matches his sheet: bare-headed curly hair, thick moustache, clean chin, broad shoulders, red drape with a gold border, white mundu hitched above bare knees. He leads two more Maravar riders through palmyra scrub and lowers his lance at a bareheaded Dutch forager in a faded blue coat. The forager raises his hands, with one leather water flask dropped and another still slung on him. There is no blood and no text. Minor points: Ponnan has a dark shoe in the stirrup where his sheet shows bare feet, and his horse is not visibly small, though there is no Nagoji in the panel to compare it with. The open sky at top right (x 0.55-1.0, y 0-0.30) holds both captions.

Clean. Night, full width: Nagoji stands alone at the waterline seen from behind in lost profile. He wears the rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, cream trousers and boots, with the talwar in his hand, and the moustache and gold ear stud are visible with a clean chin. The sea is black and heaving, the moon sits behind monsoon cloud, and nothing is on the water. The beached boats at left are on sand, not on the water. The large dark sky gives ample room for both captions.

Acceptable. The r1 fix worked. Low, narrow, dark plank boats now come in from the open sea toward the beach, bows toward the camera. Oiled, bare-chested Mukkuvar men in loincloths paddle with little spray, and the bow wakes are small. The scene is night, with monsoon cloud over a faint moon, black swells with thin foam lines, an empty beach with no Nagoji, and a palm headland at the left that matches 3.2. A large, dark, empty sky across the top half takes the caption. Minor points: the hulls are dark grey rather than truly soot-black, and a couple of paddlers grip with one hand, but neither reads as wrong at print size. Hands and anatomy are sound, and there is no text, gore or anachronism.

Clean. Nagoji matches the sheet and the chapter 13-15 row: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots and the sheet's talwar, a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin with no stubble and a small gold ear stud. The grinning fishermen are dragging a dark craft up the wet sand, and their hands and feet are sound. Nagoji walks along the beach looking toward them rather than straight at them, which still reads as an approach. There is open night sky above and right of his head for the balloon. No text, gore or anachronism.

Acceptable. Antony matches the script: lean and tall, oiled and bare-chested, loincloth only, rope scars on both forearms, a pale nick through the eyebrow, a small wooden cross on a cord and no cheek or jaw scar. He spits a thin red stream of betel juice toward the sand. One minor risk: his lips are not betel-stained, so a reader who does not know betel might take the red stream for blood. Hands are sound. A large empty night sky at the top centre and right takes both balloons. This Antony should be the reference for 3.4.

Acceptable. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch13-15 row. He wears the rust-red turban, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrists, broad red sash, cream trousers and the talwar from 3.2. He has a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a tiny flush stud on the lobe, and his hand at his chin is well drawn. The stud reads pale gold to pearl, and faint cheek shading is not stubble. The r1 fix brought Antony in line with 3.3. He has no headband, curly black hair swept back, a short grizzled beard, a pale nick through the eyebrow, rope scars on both forearms, a small wooden cross on a cord and a white loincloth, with no cheek or jaw scar. He gives a dry, unhurried shrug, hand on hip, palm flicked open toward the dark sea. Minor drift from 3.3: grey streaks in his hair, a greyer beard and a slightly heavier build. His forearm scars look like pinkish bands. He still reads as the same headman. The night beach, boats and fishermen match 3.2 and 3.3, though the figures are lit a little warmer. The wide empty sky above Nagoji's turban and right of Antony's head takes all three balloons. Hands are sound, and there is no text, gore or anachronism.

Acceptable. A towering black Dutch hull rides at anchor at night with no flag, lettering or monogram visible, only plain carved stern ornament. The cable runs down into the sea, and a dark swimmer, seen from behind and half submerged, grips it with both hands with a blade clenched crosswise in his teeth. Minor points: the cable leaves through a port near the stern quarter rather than a bow hawse, and the far end of the knife grip shows thin and pointed behind his head, but neither reads as wrong at print size. The upper-left sky with the moon and the dark hull give plenty of space for the two off-panel balloons. Their tails point to the left edge, toward the shore where Antony stands.

Acceptable. The inset matches the beat: Varma has the varma-v1 face, is bare-headed and bare-chested in a white cloth with a gold border, sits barefoot on wet black temple steps among ghee lamps with river water behind, and prays with joined hands. A separate, smaller priest tends the lamps behind him. The sappers dig at dusk with earth flying, and the Dutch flag is a correct red-white-blue tricolour. Minor: the sappers are bearded, older-looking men, and their hair is in crown knots wrapped in white cloth bands, not forward-tied kudumi. Lettering: keep both captions in the open dusk sky at top centre-right (x 0.45-0.95, y 0.02-0.20), or across the palm and sky strip at the top of the inset (x 0.25-0.43). Do not drop a box into the extreme top-left corner, where it would cover the priest's head at (0.08, 0.04).

Minor only. The sappers' topknots sit on the crown rather than tied forward. The cannon is tilted up on the rampart with slumped earth and a broken carriage under it, not buried muzzle-down, but it still reads as a sagging work. Rijtel is correct: a short, dark-haired officer in a blue coat with a sash, standing small among the sick under torn canvas, with empty barrels stacked nearby. The flag is a plain tricolour and nothing in the frame is lettered. The open dusk sky across the top takes both captions easily.

Minor only. De Lannoy points the men toward the gap rather than physically pushing them. He is seen from behind, as the script requires (no face): tall, pale-haired, in a soot-stained blue coat, standing higher than the tricorned soldiers. The thin musket puffs along the palisade and the ground-level heat haze are both there. The wide empty sky above the camp has plenty of room for the single caption.

Acceptable. It is evening under a camp awning, with Dutch fires in the distance. Ramayyan matches his sheet (thin, receding curly hair, plain white cloth, no jewellery) and stands over palm-leaf bundles with no legible writing, a leaf bundle in his hand. Varma (varma-v1 face, cream turban with jewelled crest, cream-and-gold cloth, gold necklaces) sits on a camp stool with the whetstone on his knee, sharpening a small knife, and looks toward the fires. Nagoji is in the commander look (rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar) with a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin and a small gold ear stud (a small drop, as on the sheet). Minor: the single leaf in Ramayyan's left hand reaches the lamp flame, so it could read as being held to the light. Nagoji is fully lit in the foreground rather than at the edge of the lamplight. Lettering: put Ramayyan's balloon on the awning at top centre (x 0.25-0.60, y 0.00-0.13) and Varma's on the awning and night sky at top right (x 0.62-0.95, y 0.00-0.14), above his peacock crest. Keep both clear of Nagoji's head at top left.

Minor only. Varma's forehead mark is a single red tilak rather than the white namam with a red centre line, and his hair at the nape is slightly wavy. Both match the court figure on his sheet, and the turban, peacock crest, pearl drops, thin upturned moustache and necklaces are consistent with 4.4. Ramayyan matches his sheet: receding curly hair, thin sharp face, plain white cloth, no jewellery. He is close and lit warm from the low brass lamp. Behind him, Varma's hand rests still with the knife on the whetstone. Hands are sound, and there is no painted text, balloon or anachronism. The pale awning across the top and the dark sky between the poles (x about 0.35 to 0.75, upper half) give clear space for both Ramayyan balloons, away from faces and hands.

Matches the beat: blazing sun on wet sand with heat shimmer, gunners slumped at the beach battery, one asleep against the carriage wheel, the Dutch stockade quiet beyond. No text, sound hands, and a wide clear sky band at the top for both captions. Minor: the Dutch flag is plain blue, not the chapter's plain red-white-blue tricolour (small; retouch or accept). A few Dutch blue-coats stand in the open on the beach outside their stockade. The finish is a little more painterly and less inked than panels 5.3 to 5.5.

Matches the beat and ch11 20.3: a pale hand with a sickly yellow cast and a rough cotton cuff draws in charcoal on a palm leaf on the floor of a limewashed room open to a courtyard. It shows a coastline and a small square with one corner shaded, and a brass open-wick lamp. Hand anatomy is sound. The upper wall gives clean caption space. Minor: the leaf reads somewhat like a dried board. The small island squiggles at the right edge are abstract shapes, not letters.

Nagoji matches the sheet and bible row: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots and talwar, with a thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and small gold ear stud. He has reined up on Kayal (bay, black mane, legs darkening to black, no white markings) beside a young, muscular, bare-chested Nair captain in a short white mundu with a round shield slung on his back and no turban. Hands are sound. There is open sky top centre-right for both Nagoji balloons. Minor: the captain's topknot sits on the crown, not tied forward, and he has a short beard. The Dutch flag is plain blue, not the red-white-blue tricolour.

Acceptable with a minor gunnery-logic flaw: the rammer is held from the breech side and lies along the top of the barrel instead of entering the muzzle, and the sponge is raised rather than in the bore. The beat still reads as the crew working the gun. The crouching gunner squints along the barrel with his hand on the elevation wedge, and the barrel points toward the Dutch stockade, which carries the aim beat the caption needs. Setting, white head cloths and wicker gabions match 5.5. The Dutch flag is a plain tricolour with no text. The caption fits in the clear upper-right sky.

Clean against the sheets. Nagoji wears the commander look (rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash over the shoulder and round the waist, cream trousers, boots, talwar) with a thick curled moustache, clean-shaven chin and small gold ear ornament, matching nagoji-v2. Kayal is a bay with a black mane, tail and lower legs and no white markings, on the quilted ochre pad. The gun fires with a white smoke puff, and dust at the wheels suggests recoil. Minor: the gunner with the lit linstock stands right of the muzzle instead of at the breech, which is odd but not dangerous-looking given the perspective. The battery, gabions and crew dress match 5.4. There is no text or pseudo-text, and the clear upper-centre and right sky holds both captions.

Minor only. A sand plume from another shot already rises inside the Dutch camp, though the ball is clearly still in flight. The ball has a white comic contrail. Our battery flag is plain red with no silver conch. The beat reads: the ball is a dark speck in a hard blue sky, arcing over the Dutch stockade and the tents where the sick lie on cots. The upper-right sky is clear for the 6.2 inset, and the caption fits in the open sky at upper centre. There is no text in the art.

Clean. The stone church storehouse has a fresh ragged hole in its tiled roof, with dust and debris sifting down onto the powder barrels stacked in the doorway beside the rice sacks. A single blue-coated VOC soldier stares up at the hole. A small iron candle cresset by the door is harmless. The caption sits in the sky at upper left.

Acceptable, and it fixes the r1 failure. Nagoji matches the sheet and the ch14 row: compact rust-red turban, long curly black hair, a thick black moustache with curled ends, a clean-shaven chin with no stubble, a small gold stud bead on the lobe, cream tunic with sleeves to the wrist, broad red sash with the loose end whipping back, cream trousers, boots and a talwar hilt. Kayal is correct: a bay coat with black mane, tail and lower legs and no white markings, the ochre quilted pad, and she is rearing. His right fist hauls on the reins and his left hand is hidden. The blast glare, the flame-and-smoke pillar and the spinning debris sit over the Dutch stockade, and the forward gabion trench is full of men flat with their hands over their heads. The hard blue sky matches 6.1. There is no text, no gore and no anachronism, and the panel needs no lettering space. One flaw: at the far left edge, behind our cannon (about x 0 to 0.075, y 0.38 to 0.45), two small background figures wear blue coats and black tricornes. They read as Dutch soldiers inside our battery and contradict the bare-chested Nair gun crews in white turbans of 5.1 to 5.5. They are small and partly hidden by the cannon and the flying sash. A paint-out to white-turbaned Nair gunners, or a slight crop of the left edge, is recommended if a retouch pass is available.

Acceptable, with small deviations. Dhanaji is mounted on his own bay beside Nagoji rather than standing at his stirrup, but he is lower and shouting up at him, so the beat reads. He matches his sheet: white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, short black beard, dust on his face. Nagoji has a curled moustache, a clean chin and a gold stud on the lobe, though his turban is fuller than compact. Continuity with 6.3 is a little soft: the blast pillar has thinned to drifting grey smoke and the background gunners are calmly serving their guns. Place Dhanaji's wavering balloon in the smoky sky at upper right, with the tail down to his mouth, and the caption in the sky at upper centre.

Acceptable. Fire sweeps the full length of the stockade with secondary explosions, and the figures are tiny and far. The deviations are small. The sky is overcast grey, unlike the hard blue of 6.1, which reads as the smoke pall. The running figures are on the open sand outside the stockade rather than between the burning huts. A plain white flag stands over our lines at far left and could be misread as a surrender flag. Both captions fit in the low-detail grey sky at upper left. There is no text or gore.

Minor only: the Nair extras in the foreground trench wear their topknots on the crown rather than forward-tied. Otherwise the beat is right: blue- and grey-coated Dutch ranks with fixed bayonets and levelled muskets step out of the burning palisade, the tricolour is plain, there is no text, and the palm grove on the left gives Dhanaji's off-panel tail a place to point (left edge). The open sky at upper left and centre takes the balloon.

Minor only: the rendering is more painterly than the inked look of 7.1, 7.3 and 7.5. One Nair extra cut off at the left edge wears a white head cloth, and the topknots sit on the crown rather than forward-tied. The beat reads clearly: a distant Dutch line fires a volley in a long bank of smoke, and in the foreground trench men duck behind shields at the wicker parapet. There is no gore and no text, and the large clear sky at upper left takes the caption.

Ramayyan matches his sheet: thin, sharp features, receding crown with curly sides, bare-headed, no shield, a mud-splattered white dhoti and a curved sword raised. He is bare-chested, which the script allows because it names only the dhoti. Nair topknots sit on the crown rather than forward-tied (minor, extras). The Dutch bayonets press against the shield wall with no blood, the flags are plain tricolours, and hands and anatomy are sound. The clear sky at upper left and centre, above the embankment, takes both short balloons.

Acceptable. Nagoji matches his sheet: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots, talwar, thick curled moustache, clean chin (only faint skin shading on the jaw, no stubble) and a small gold ear stud. He rides Kayal, the taller bay with a black mane. Dhanaji (white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, short black beard) is at his shoulder. Ponnan is bare-headed with curly hair, thick moustache, clean chin, red shoulder cloth and white mundu above bare knees, on a smaller horse a head lower. The sky at upper right is clear for the caption. Minor issues: the grove is sunlit rather than in deep shade, and Nagoji leans forward only slightly. Two background Deccan riders wear white turbans with indigo quilted tunics and beards, so they echo Dhanaji. Ponnan's short jacket is olive-brown where his sheet tunic is red; the bible does not fix the colour. The distant Dutch position at right reads as a stone fort with towers and a calm tent camp, not the burning wooden stockade of 7.5. It is hazy and small.

Clean. The view is from a rise at the palm line (palm trunk and rocks in the foreground), looking down at the Dutch square. Its front is jammed against the packed Nair line at left, its rear rank faces the burning palisade, and the near flank facing the scrubland is a single ragged file with daylight between the men. An officer at right reaches out and pulls a soldier from that file toward the front. There is no text or flag lettering, and the large clear sky at upper left takes both captions.

Minor only. Nagoji matches the sheet: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, boots, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud. Kayal is correct: bay, black mane, black lower legs. Dhanaji is correct: white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, short beard. A second background rider in the same indigo quilted tunic and white turban, also bearded, just right of Dhanaji could be taken for him at a glance. The distant stone fort and town match the 7.4 background but not the wooden palisade in 8.2 to 8.5. Both captions fit the clear sky at upper right (x 0.68 to 0.98, y 0.03 to 0.25).

Minor: a few white-turbaned riders on the left are drawn slightly ahead of the POV rider rather than behind, which still reads as one charging wave. Kayal's ears and black mane match the sheet. The sergeant has his mouth open and his arm out with a sound five-fingered hand. Bayonets sit at scattered angles, and the burning stockade behind the square matches 6.5 and 7.5. No text. The open blue sky at upper left is clear space for the caption.

Minor only. The impact beat is clear: a horse rears into the blue-coat block, Dutch soldiers go down in dust, hats and a musket drop to the sand, with no blood. The Dutch flag at the far right edge is plain dark blue rather than the red-white-blue tricolour, but it has no lettering and is cut off by the frame. Nair infantry fill the left foreground, though the script stages only our horse hitting the flank. That is plausible after 7.5, where the square's front ranks were pressed against the Nair line. The caption fits the sky at upper left (x 0.03 to 0.4, y 0.0 to 0.15).

Minor only. Dhanaji (white pagdi, indigo quilted tunic, short black beard, talwar raised) rides nearly abreast of Nagoji, slightly forward and nearer the camera, not a clear half length ahead. The Dutch beyond are three soldiers standing close together facing away in the dust, not strictly back to back. Kayal has a faint pale sheen on the forehead that is a highlight, not a real white star; the clear star belongs to Dhanaji's brown horse, which is allowed. Nagoji matches the sheet: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash (its loose end lies across his thigh and is cloth, not blood), cream trousers, boots, talwar, curled moustache, clean-shaven chin, small gold ear stud. Fallen Dutch soldiers show no blood. No text. The smoky sky at top centre, above and between the two heads, has room for the caption.

Minor: the musket already lies in the trampled sand rather than falling, which still reads as dropped. The surrendering Dutch, out of focus with hands up, are seen mostly from behind, so no faces can be read. A small post with a crossbar stands among the burning stockade towers in the background; it is negligible. The warm late light and the burning stockade carry over from 8.2 and 8.4 and lead into the 9.1 sunset. No text, no blood. The soft cloud at top centre and the open foreground sand both have room for the caption.

Only v02 was offered and it is acceptable. It matches the 9.1 beat: a wide lurid purple-red sunset through smoke, the stockade burned down to glowing embers along the dune, and Dutch survivors in ash-stained blue coats on the beach, some kneeling and some standing with hands raised. The setting is the open beach, which fits 8.5 and 9.2. There is no painted text, no blood and no noose. Small points only: the shirtless Nair guard in the right foreground has a cluster of three spear or staff shafts near him, and his grip is a little ambiguous. Dutch ships sit on the horizon, which fits the historical siege. Neither problem touches a principal or the key action. The upper-left sky, above the horizon and left of the smoke, is clear and low in detail for the caption.

Acceptable. This is a waist-up close shot of De Lannoy, steady and unflinching, matching his sheet (pale hair with black ribbon, standing collar, torn, soot-stained blue coat). His hands are sound. Minor issue: he looks toward screen right, although Ramayyan stood to his left in 9.3, which is a small screen-direction flip. Lettering space: the large sunset sky at upper right (x 0.5 to 0.98, y 0.02 to 0.35).

Acceptable. Nagoji matches the sheet and the chapter 14 row: rust-red turban, cream tunic, broad red sash, cream trousers, boots and a talwar at the sash. He has a thick curled moustache, a clean-shaven chin with no stubble, and a small gold ear stud, and he watches De Lannoy with narrowed eyes. Kayal is a bay with a black mane and tail, darkening lower legs, an ochre quilted pad and no white markings. Nagoji is set apart from the group with the smoking palisade behind, consistent with 9.2 to 9.4. Lettering space: the smoke-filled sky at top centre (x 0.25 to 0.65, y 0.02 to 0.3) and the sunset at top left.

Minor only. Nagoji matches the sheet: rust-red turban, cream tunic, red sash, boots, talwar, thick curled moustache, clean chin, gold ear stud. Kayal is a correct bay with black points. Ramayyan matches his sheet: receding hair, thin, mud-and-soot-splattered white cloth. He sheathes the sword with the wiping cloth in his other hand. The sword reads as straight with a crossguard and ball pommel rather than the curved Nair sword, and its hilt differs from the sheathed sword in 10.2. The wiping cloth is a plain dark red, not blood. The background Nair guards have loose curly hair rather than forward-tied topknots. Clear twilight sky at top left (caption), right of Nagoji's head (his balloon) and above Ramayyan (his balloon).

Minor only. Varma matches varma-v1 in the campaign court look (cream-and-gold turban with peacock crest, bare chest, cream-gold cloth, gold necklaces) and is mounted, looking past the group toward the huddled Dutch prisoners and the departing ships. Ramayyan is in the foreground with his sword sheathed, looking toward the king. The Nair captain stands at the stirrup, looking up, with bare chest, short white mundu, round shield and spear, and no turban. His topknot is tied at the back of the crown, not forward-tied (kudumi). The sheathed sword's hilt and curve differ from 10.1. Large clear sky at upper right for the captain's balloon.
Clean against sheets, bible row and script beat.

Minor only. Varma, in the same turban, crest and cream-gold cloth as 10.2, rides away and twists back in the saddle to speak over his shoulder. His hands and anatomy are sound. Nagoji (moustache, clean chin, gold stud, boots, talwar) and Ramayyan (receding hair, splattered dhoti, sheathed sword and palm-leaf bundle) watch him go. Nagoji is now dismounted after riding up in 10.1, and Kayal is not shown. Varma heads toward the surf rather than clearly inland off the beach. There is faint jaw shading on Nagoji that reads as shadow, not stubble, at print size. Clear dusk sky above and right of Varma for both balloons.

Acceptable with deviations. This is the full-width closer: a smoking, burning fort ruin under a last red sky, and Dutch prisoners walking in file with wrists bound in front and no ropes at the neck, guarded by spearmen. Nagoji matches the sheet (moustache, clean chin, gold stud, compact turban, sash). Kayal is a correct bay with black points, apart from a tiny forehead highlight that does not read as a marking. Nagoji and Kayal are fully lit and mid-sized, not a small silhouette against the ruin as scripted. The spearmen wear loose hair and shoulder cloths rather than forward topknots and bare chests. The fort here shows stone walls under the palisade, where 10.1, 10.2 and 10.4 show an earthen slope. The large clear red sky at top left and top centre holds all three captions.
